experiment.title: Would you notice it is not MongoDB?
experiment.note: Written, hashed and published before the counted run. Nothing in this record may change after publication; a later change is a new, dated amendment, refuted and published first.
experiment.summary: On the operations Odin actually performs on document-shaped data, does a permissively licensed wire layer over PostgreSQL (FerretDB 2.7.0 with DocumentDB) answer exactly like MongoDB Community 9.0.2, as seen by the official driver?

freeze.rule: Frozen at publication: the operations, arms, corpus, comparator, controls, P1 and the decision rule. The runner that executes the frozen corpus is published by amendment 01 before any counted run (the EXP 008 precedent); the amendment may add only the runner and the O20/O21 capability rows, and its merge sets the not-before.

question: Odin needs a document store it owns. If a wire-compatible layer under permissive licences already answers like MongoDB on the operations Odin uses, owning means adopting and forking it; if it does not, the gap is what Odin would have to build.

cleanRoom.statement: Commands are written from public documentation only; no MongoDB server source, test file or specification text is in this repository. The reference server is run, not read.

operations.name: insertOne / insertMany, unordered, with a per-item result
operations.evidence: memory-service create path and its non-transactional batch endpoint (per-item 201/207)

operations.name: replaceOne with upsert (whole document)
operations.evidence: memory-service write replaces the whole value

operations.name: findOne by _id
operations.evidence: memory-service read by (namespace, key)

operations.name: find with $eq / anchored $regex prefix on top-level fields, $gte/$lte on timestamps
operations.evidence: memory-service query filter: namespace prefix, key, owner, time ranges

operations.name: find with $eq on a nested field
operations.evidence: one database-side compare-and-set guard; otherwise emulated in application code

operations.name: find with $in / $all array membership
operations.evidence: dependency membership and role containment queries

operations.name: sort + limit + skip, countDocuments, cursor batches
operations.evidence: memory-service pagination with a total count; relational take/skip/orderBy

operations.name: updateOne $set on a nested path
operations.evidence: rare: one nested JSON set on a policy document

operations.name: updateOne $inc
operations.evidence: version counters and access counters

operations.name: updateOne $addToSet
operations.evidence: membership arrays appended only when absent

operations.name: $push / $pull
operations.evidence: not found in current code

operations.name: findOneAndUpdate as compare-and-set on a version
operations.evidence: conditional update with a version increment; one store does it non-atomically today

operations.name: aggregate $group + $count
operations.evidence: memory-service stats by namespace prefix and owner; relational groupBy

operations.name: aggregate $facet / $lookup
operations.evidence: not found in current code

operations.name: createIndex single-field and compound, unique, hint
operations.evidence: metadata indexes; unique (namespace, key)

operations.name: partial unique index
operations.evidence: unique (tenant, external id) only where the id is present

operations.name: vector search (HNSW cosine)
operations.evidence: pgvector in the memory service and the agent memory store
operations.why: MongoDB Community serves vector search through a separate search process; a capability check, not a wire-compatibility case.

operations.name: text index / $text
operations.evidence: search runs in an application-side index, not the database

operations.name: TTL index
operations.evidence: expiry is an application sweep today (and collides with append-only)

operations.name: change stream with a resume token
operations.evidence: only a non-durable in-process feed exists; this is a wanted capability

operations.name: multi-document transaction
operations.evidence: relational transactions writing a row and its audit row together

operations.name: advisory / pessimistic lock
operations.evidence: a transaction-scoped advisory lock
operations.why: No MongoDB equivalent; an application-level primitive.

operations.name: database-enforced append-only collections
operations.evidence: a trigger refuses update and delete on audit namespaces

operations.name: per-document version history, rollback and diff
operations.evidence: a history row per version with rollback and diff endpoints

operations.name: key-order-preserving storage of hashed payloads
operations.evidence: a decision record requires the hashed payload be stored as text because JSONB reorders keys
operations.measuredBy: cases O01-03 and O01-04 (key order and numeric types survive a round trip)

operations.name: per-tenant database or schema isolation
operations.evidence: one database per tenant; one schema per memory instance

reference.licence: SSPL-1.0 (run unmodified as a black box; not redistributed)
reference.topology: single-node replica set (so sessions, transactions and change streams exist)

candidate.topology: one FerretDB process in front of one PostgreSQL 17 with the DocumentDB extension, default settings

corpus.authoring: 61 commands written on 2026-10-10 from the public documentation pages each case links; every case runs on a freshly dropped database (setup commands, then the measured command), with explicit _id values so no server-generated value enters a reply. Written before either server was run.

normalisation: volatile envelope fields dropped: $clusterTime, operationTime, electionId, opTime, lastCommittedOpTime, $configTime, $topologyTime, readOnly, errmsg
errors compared by ok, code and codeName; per-document write errors by index, code and codeName
a non-zero cursor id becomes "<open>"; 0 stays 0
reply envelopes compared as maps; returned documents (cursor batches, findAndModify value) compared with key order significant
types compared exactly (canonical Extended JSON v2)
a batch is a multiset only when its case declares unordered: true
comparator.teeth: scripts/document-store-compare.test.mjs: 12 planted divergences in a returned batch plus error, write-error and findAndModify mutations must each be reported; volatile fields, envelope key order, errmsg text and an open cursor's id value must not be.

controls.positive: Reference against itself: the full corpus is run twice against two fresh reference containers; every case must compare equal.
controls.negative: Planted divergence: for every case, the runner also compares the reference reply against a copy with one deterministic, observable mutation (the first returned document's first non-_id value's type changed, or for replies without documents, ok flipped); every one must be reported as different.
controls.calibrationBar: If the positive control shows any difference, or the negative control misses any mutation, the comparator is miscalibrated: the run is void, published as void, and P1 is not computed.

P1.claim: The candidate is indistinguishable from the reference on at least 95% of the cases that exercise operations Odin uses today.
P1.metric: indistinguishable cases / used cases, each case compared once after one execution per arm
P1.interval: Wilson 95% interval reported beside the point estimate; the decision uses the point estimate as pre-registered here

decision.rule: P1 >= 0.95: adopt the candidate as the base of an Odin-owned store (fork, spec, governance layer). 0.80 <= P1 < 0.95: adopt and build the failing operation classes. P1 < 0.80: adoption is refuted for Odin's needs; stay on PostgreSQL JSONB and treat building a wire layer as the open question.
decision.refutedBy: P1 < 0.95 refutes the claim; the band it falls in selects the decision.

secondary.what: Per operation class: indistinguishable share, with every divergent case published with its comparator reason.
The 6 cases on operations Odin does not use today (O11, O14, O18, O19), reported separately, never pooled into P1.

Change streams (O20) and multi-document transactions (O21): does the candidate accept the command at all, and do events/commits match? Reported as capability rows; added to the corpus by amendment 01 with the runner, because they need sessions and a tailing cursor.
Descriptive latency: median wall time per case per arm on the same runner. No claim; one runner, one execution.

execution.where: A GitHub Actions runner in this public repository, both arms as service containers pinned by digest; never an operator laptop.
execution.runner: scripts/document-store-run.mjs, published by amendment 01 before any counted run; it executes this frozen corpus and comparator unchanged.
execution.notBefore: The merge time of amendment 01 in this repository; no counted run before it.
execution.environment: Node 22, the pinned driver installed from the frozen lockfile; one counted run; a failed run is published as failed, never retried silently.

spend.statement: No model call and no paid service: two pinned container images on a standard runner.

limits: One version of each server, default settings, single node; no claim about sharding, failover or performance at scale.
The corpus covers the operations Odin uses today as found on 2026-10-10; it is not a general compatibility suite and a high P1 says nothing about operations outside it.
Commands are compared through one driver (Node.js); other drivers can expose differences this one hides.
The reference is MongoDB's behaviour, not a specification: where MongoDB's own behaviour is a bug, the candidate is still scored against it.
The source studied (r8.3.11) and the reference binary (9.0.2) differ: 9.0.2 has no public source tag yet. Behavioural claims are taken from the binary's replies, not the notes.

sources.claim: FerretDB 2.7.0, Apache-2.0, works best with DocumentDB v0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0
9.0.2 is a production release; the Community macOS arm64 build sha256 9a30e942...6de3 was verified before inspection
